diagnostic_evidence.quote: By convention, the inner product $\Dotp{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Hilb}$ is linear in the first argument.

issues.failure_explanation: With the stated convention (linear in the first slot) and $(\Bentry{h}\Tensor{X})(\mIndex{i}) = \Bentry{h}x_{\mIndex{i}}$, the left side equals $\sum_{\mIndex{i}}\overline{x_{\mIndex{i}}}\,\langle \Bentry{a}_{\mIndex{i}},\Bentry{h}\rangle_{\Hilb}$ while the right side equals $\sum_{\mIndex{i}}x_{\mIndex{i}}\,\langle \Bentry{a}_{\mIndex{i}},\Bentry{h}\rangle_{\Hilb}$. The identity holds only for real $x_{\mIndex{i}}$, so it is false for $\F = \Clx$; the variational step and the identification of the two maxima that follow it are therefore not obtained as written (the paper handles the conjugation correctly in Lemma lem:added-4).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Conjugate the rank-one factor in the identity (replace $\Bentry{a}(\Tensor{X})$ by $\Bentry{a}(\overline{\Tensor{X}})$, or $\Tensor{X}$ by $\overline{\Tensor{X}}$ on the left) and add the one-line observation that $\Tensor{X}\mapsto\overline{\Tensor{X}}$ is a bijection on the rank-one tensors inside the maximum; no statement or bound changes.
issues.overall_effect: Over complex Hilbert spaces item 3 of Lemma lemma:norms_are_norms is unproved, so the dual representation of the spectral norm is unavailable; the proofs of items 3 and 6 of Lemma lem:added-4 and, through the norm equivalence they supply, of Theorem theorem:bochner_hilbert_space inherit the gap. All statements remain true.
issues.title: Missing conjugation in the proof of the dual formula for the spectral norm
issues.why_classification: One conjugation plus a one-line remark repairs the proof and leaves every statement, hypothesis and guarantee untouched, so the repair is short, local and routine with no mathematical loss.

issues.failure_explanation: For $x \in \mathbb{M}$ one has $\Matrix{C}x \in \Kernel{c}{\Batrix{A}\Matrix{B}}$ but not necessarily $\Matrix{C}x \in \Kernel{}{\Matrix{B}}^\perp$. Concrete counterexample (valid already for $\Hilb = \F$, with $\Batrix{A} = 0$): $\Matrix{B} = \mathrm{diag}(1,0)$, $\Matrix{C} = [1\ 0;1\ 1]$ give $\mathbb{M} = \mathbb{L} = \mathrm{span}\{e_1\}$ but $\Matrix{C}e_1 = (1,1)^{\trans} \notin \mathbb{L}$. Hence the asserted operator $\Linop{C}:\mathbb{M}\to\mathbb{L}$ does not exist and the estimate $\dim\Image{}{\Linop{C}} \leq \dim\mathbb{L}$ is unsupported, leaving the Frobenius inequality (and Sylvester's inequality derived from it) unproved as written.

failure_location.quote: Consider $\Matrix{x} \mapsto \Matrix{Cx}$ as an injective linear operator $\Linop{C} : \mathbb{M} \to \mathbb{L}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $\Matrix{x}\mapsto\Matrix{Cx}$ by $\Matrix{x}\mapsto\Pi\Matrix{C}\Matrix{x}$, where $\Pi$ is the orthogonal projection onto $\Kernel{}{\Matrix{B}}^\perp$. This map is injective on $\mathbb{M}$ (its kernel meets $\mathbb{M}$ inside $\Kernel{}{\Matrix{BC}}\cap\mathbb{M}=0$) and lands in $\mathbb{L}$ because $\Matrix{B}\Pi\Matrix{C}x = \Matrix{B}\Matrix{C}x$ and $\Batrix{A}\Matrix{B}\Matrix{C}x=0$; the dimension count then goes through unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Parts 2 and 3 of Lemma lemma:rank_nullity are unestablished; the rank equalities of Lemma lemma:rank_properties, Lemma lemma:singular_values_connection, Theorem thm:added-1 and, through Theorem theorem:truncated_svd, the results Corolary corolalry:lowrank_set_closed, Corollary corollary:oneside_approximation_via_projection and Theorem theorem:bochner_hosvd rest on that unproved step.
issues.title: Frobenius-inequality proof uses a map that leaves the claimed target subspace
issues.why_classification: The inequality itself is correct and the repair replaces one operator in the proof by its composition with a standard orthogonal projection, after which the same two-line dimension count works; every statement, hypothesis and guarantee is preserved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Note that $\Matrix{B}^\pinv \Matrix{B} = \Matrix{I}_{m}$ and $\Matrix{C} \Matrix{C}^\pinv = \Matrix{I}_{n}$, then substitute $\Matrix{C}^\pinv \Batrix{A}^\pinv \Matrix{B}^\pinv$ into Theorem~\ref{theorem:pinv_bochner}.
The matrix of $\Batrix{A}^\pinv$ in the standard basis $\{ \Matrix{e}_i \}$ coincides with the pseudoinverse of the corresponding usual matrix.

issues.failure_explanation: Substituting the candidate into the four Penrose equations verifies only the two absorption equations; the self-adjointness conditions fail. The claim is false already for $\Hilb = \F$ (where $\Batrix{A}^\pinv$ is the usual pseudoinverse): take $\Matrix{B} = [1\ 0;0\ 1;1\ 1]$ (full column rank), $\Matrix{C} = \Matrix{I}_2$ (full row rank), $\Batrix{A} = [1\ 0;0\ 0]$. Then $\Matrix{B}\Batrix{A}\Matrix{C} = [1\ 0;0\ 0;1\ 0]$ has pseudoinverse $\tfrac12[1\ 0\ 1;0\ 0\ 0]$, whereas $\Matrix{C}^\pinv\Batrix{A}^\pinv\Matrix{B}^\pinv = \tfrac13[2\ -1\ 1;0\ 0\ 0]$; the two products differ and $(\Matrix{B}\Batrix{A}\Matrix{C})(\Matrix{C}^\pinv\Batrix{A}^\pinv\Matrix{B}^\pinv)$ is not symmetric.

failure_location.quote: If $\Matrix{B} \in \F^{k \times m}$ has full column rank and $\Matrix{C} \in \F^{n \times l}$ has full row rank, $(\Matrix{B} \Batrix{A} \Matrix{C})^\pinv = \Matrix{C}^\pinv \Batrix{A}^\pinv \Matrix{B}^\pinv$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the hypotheses, e.g. require $\Matrix{B}$ to have orthonormal columns and $\Matrix{C}$ to have orthonormal rows (so $\Matrix{B}^\pinv = \Matrix{B}^\ast$, $\Matrix{C}^\pinv = \Matrix{C}^\ast$ and both self-adjointness conditions hold), or require the middle factor to have full rank equal to the linking dimension; the identity cannot hold for arbitrary full-rank $\Matrix{B},\Matrix{C}$.
issues.overall_effect: Item 2 of Lemma lem:added-8 is false on its stated domain, so the advertised transfer of the pseudoinverse product rule to Bochner matrices fails. No other result relies on this identity: Lemma lemma:cur_column uses only the special factorisation case, which is valid and is derivable from Lemma lemma:pinv_full_rank.
issues.title: Pseudoinverse of a three-factor product is not the product of the pseudoinverses
issues.why_classification: The statement is false as quantified and no local edit saves it: hypotheses must be restricted (or the identity replaced), which narrows the advertised generality while leaving a recognisable pseudoinverse product rule; the loss exceeds a routine fix but no new proof architecture is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The sets $\mathbb{M}_{\leq \kappa}$ and $\mathbb{M}_{\preccurlyeq (\rho,\kappa)} = \set{\Batrix{B} \in \Hilb^{m \times n}}{\Rank{T}{\Batrix{B}} \preccurlyeq (\rho,\kappa)}$ are closed.
The column rank of $\Batrix{C}_\ast$ is bounded by $\kappa$, so it cannot be a better column-side approximant of $\Batrix{A}$ than $\scup{svd}_\kappa(\Batrix{A})$:
We denote by $\Hilb$ a Hilbert space over $\F$.

issues.failure_explanation: For the infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces the paper allows, closedness of $\mathbb{M}_{\preccurlyeq (\rho,\kappa)}$ does not imply that a continuous objective attains its infimum: bounded sets of $\Hilb^{m\times n}$ are not compact and the low-rank set is not convex, so a minimizing sequence need not converge. The minimizer $\Batrix{C}_\ast$ is then used essentially to derive the $\sqrt{2}$ quasioptimality constant, which is therefore not established as written.

failure_location.quote: Since $\mathbb{M}_{\preccurlyeq (\rho,\kappa)}$ is closed, there is a minimizer $\Batrix{C}_\ast \in \mathbb{M}_{\preccurlyeq (\rho,\kappa)}$ of $\Norm{\Batrix{A} - \Batrix{C}}{\ell_2(\Hilb)}$ over $\mathbb{M}_{\preccurlyeq (\rho,\kappa)}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either replace the appeal to closedness by an attainment argument (write $\Batrix{C}=\Matrix{D}\Batrix{F}\Matrix{C}$ of rank $(\rho,\kappa)$, note that for fixed $\Matrix{D},\Matrix{C}$ the optimal $\Batrix{F}$ solves a least-squares problem and that $\Matrix{D},\Matrix{C}$ range over compact sets), or state the bound with $\inf$ and derive it from a minimizing sequence with an $\varepsilon$-argument; the constant $\sqrt{2}$ and all conclusions survive.
issues.overall_effect: The quasioptimality bound with constant $\sqrt{2}$ in Theorem theorem:bochner_hosvd is unsupported as written for infinite-dimensional $\Hilb$ (the statement and the first error bound are unaffected).
issues.title: Existence of the best Tucker approximant inferred from closedness alone
issues.why_classification: A short limiting argument (or a short attainment remark) replaces one sentence and leaves the statement, the constant and every guarantee intact, so no substantive claim or regime is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Its solution can be represented as
In our experiment, we choose $\alpha_{\max} = \beta_{\max} = 2$, $m = n = 100$, and $K = 75$.

issues.failure_explanation: What the prose claims: the sine series with coefficients $u_k = \frac{k[1-(-1)^k\cos(\beta\pi)]}{(k^2+\alpha^2)(k^2+\beta^2)}$ solves eq:ode_bvp and hence represents the solution map to be approximated. What is true: expanding $\cos(\beta x)$ in the sine basis gives $b_k = \frac{2}{\pi}\frac{k[1-(-1)^k\cos(\beta\pi)]}{k^2-\beta^2}$, and $-u''-\alpha^2 u$ multiplies the $k$th sine mode by $(k^2-\alpha^2)$, so the coefficients must be $u_k = \frac{k[1-(-1)^k\cos(\beta\pi)]}{(k^2-\alpha^2)(k^2-\beta^2)}$. (For $\alpha=1/2,\beta=0$ the exact solution $u=4(\cos(x/2)+\sin(x/2)-1)$ has $u_1=8/3$, while the displayed formula gives $u_1=8/5$.) The difference: the section computes with a map that is not the solution map of eq:ode_bvp; moreover, with the correct coefficients the stated problem has no solution for $\alpha\in\{1,2\}$ (resonance of $-u''-\alpha^2$ at $k=\alpha$), and $\alpha=2$ is one of the 100 grid values.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Make the operator and the series consistent and regenerate the data: either replace $(k^2+\alpha^2)(k^2+\beta^2)$ by $(k^2-\alpha^2)(k^2-\beta^2)$ and remove the resonant values $\alpha\in\{1,2\}$ from the parameter grid (changing $\alpha_{\max}$ or the grid), or replace $-u''-\alpha^2 u$ by the coercive $-u''+\alpha^2 u$ and replace $(k^2+\beta^2)$ by $(k^2-\beta^2)$; in both cases the Fourier data behind Figure fig:ode_bvp must be recomputed.
issues.overall_effect: All statements of Section 6.1 about approximating 'the solution map' of eq:ode_bvp are unsupported as written, and the advertised parameter box $[0,2]\times[0,2]$ is incompatible with the stated operator (the truncated maps behind Figure fig:ode_bvp are built from the wrong series).
issues.title: Displayed series is not the solution of the stated boundary-value problem
issues.why_classification: The two consistent repairs differ mathematically and neither is forced, so this is not a typo; keeping the stated operator forces the advertised box $[0,2]^2$ to lose the resonant $\alpha$-values, and any repair requires regenerating the numerical evidence. The method and its qualitative conclusions survive recognisably, so the loss is limited rather than major.
